title: SyRI welfare fraud-detection system halted by court
summary: The District Court of The Hague ruled the SyRI legislation (Systeem Risico Indicatie) unlawful for breaching Article 8 ECHR: the opaque, inter-agency data-linkage risk model targeted low-income neighbourhoods and lacked sufficient safeguards, with a risk of discrimination by socio-economic and migration background. The system was halted.
notes: Judgment: District Court of The Hague, ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2020:865 (English ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2020:1878).

title: Clearview AI — untargeted scraping of facial images in France
summary: CNIL order (MED-2021-134, 26 November 2021, made public 6 December 2021) finding Clearview AI unlawfully collected and processed facial images of people in France without a legal basis to build a facial-recognition database sold to law enforcement.
notes: Order of 26 November 2021, made public 6 December 2021.

title: ChatGPT data breach exposing users' conversations and payment data
summary: On 20 March 2023 a ChatGPT bug exposed other users' chat histories and partial payment details; the breach was cited by the Garante in its 31 March 2023 action against OpenAI, alongside the absence of a legal basis for training-data collection and of age verification.
source_title: Garante, 31 Mar 2023: Artificial intelligence: stop to ChatGPT by the Italian SA
notes: Breach cited by the Garante in its 31 March 2023 action against OpenAI.

title: Grok sexualised deepfakes disseminated on X
summary: The Commission found the risks of Grok's functionalities deployed into X "seem to have materialised", with manipulated sexually explicit images — including content that may amount to child sexual abuse material — disseminated in the EU, exposing citizens to serious harm.

title: Dutch childcare benefits scandal (Toeslagenaffaire) — nationality-based risk profiling
summary: The parliamentary inquiry report 'Ongekend onrecht' (17 December 2020) found the Tax Administration's childcare-benefit fraud approach used a risk model that included a self-learning algorithm with (dual) nationality as an indicator. Around 26,000 families were wrongly accused of fraud and faced full recovery of benefits; the approach ran from about 2005 to 2019, and the cabinet resigned on 15 January 2021.
source_title: Tweede Kamer, Kamerstukken II 2020/21, 35 510, nr. 2 — 'Ongekend onrecht'
notes: Risk profiling ran about 2005–2019; around 26,000 families wrongly accused; cabinet resigned 15 January 2021.

title: Clearview AI — untargeted scraping of facial images including Greek residents
summary: A complaint by Homo Digitalis on behalf of a Greek resident (right of access) led the Hellenic Data Protection Authority to find that Clearview AI had collected facial images of Greek residents without a legal basis to build a facial-recognition database.
notes: Dated to the complaint of 26 May 2021 (G/IN/3458/26-05-2021); the Authority's decision followed on 13 July 2022.

title: Swedish Police Authority's unlawful use of Clearview AI facial recognition
summary: The Swedish Police Authority used Clearview AI's facial-recognition app from autumn 2019 to 3 March 2020 without a lawful basis, in breach of the Criminal Data Act; the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY) found the use unlawful.
source_title: Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY), 11 Feb 2021
notes: Dated to 3 March 2020, the last day of the documented use period; IMY decision DI-2020-2719 of 10 February 2021.
